Eight publications across ICML, ICLR and CVPR workshops. Two were selected as orals and two are indexed in PMLR.

  • The Geometry of Forgetting: A Fisher-Information Framework for Alignment-Preserving Continual Adaptation oral ICML 2026 · CATS workshop. Uses Fisher information to identify which parameter directions carry a model's alignment, then constrains continual fine-tuning to leave them alone. The model keeps learning new tasks without eroding the safety behaviour it started with.
  • Unsupervised Detection of Speculative Regimes and the Empirical Audit of Agentic Responsibility in Financial Markets ICLR 2026 · Advances in Financial AI workshop. Detects the periods where a market stops behaving the way it usually does, with no labelled examples to train on, then audits how much of that behaviour traces back to autonomous trading agents.
  • Tensor-SAE: Structured Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable and Efficient Image Representations PMLR ICLR 2026 · GRaM workshop. Imposes tensor structure on a sparse autoencoder's dictionary so features pulled from an image model keep their spatial and channel layout. Cheaper to train and easier to interpret than a flat SAE.
  • Learning Compact Representations via Intrinsic Dimension Regularization PMLR ICLR 2026 · GRaM workshop. Adds a penalty pushing a network's learned representation toward lower intrinsic dimension. The result is a compact embedding that keeps the structure that matters and discards the rest.
  • ShapeUQ: Propagating 3D Reconstruction Uncertainty Through Scientific PDE Simulations via Shape Calculus oral CVPR 2026 · 3D4S workshop. Propagates the uncertainty in a 3D reconstruction forward through the PDE simulations run on top of it, using shape calculus. Shows how much of a simulation result is really reconstruction error.
  • Conformal Semantic Communication: Distribution-Free Task-Level Coverage Guarantees for Goal-Oriented Transmission Under Channel Shift ICML 2026 · AI4NextG workshop. Gives a receiver a coverage guarantee on the task-level meaning it recovers rather than on the raw bits. The guarantee holds when the channel shifts, with no distribution assumed.
  • Distribution-Free Adaptive Modulation and Coding via Online Conformal Inference under Non-Stationary Fading ICML 2026 · AI4NextG workshop. Selects modulation and coding online through conformal inference, so the reliability target holds as the fading channel drifts. Nothing about the channel distribution has to be assumed in advance.
  • Spectral Dynamics of Low-Rank Adaptation: Rank Monotonicity, Implicit Bias, and Optimal Rank Selection in LoRA and Tucker Fine-Tuning CoLoRAI workshop. Tracks how the singular values of LoRA and Tucker updates evolve during fine-tuning and the implicit bias that follows. Turns rank selection into a rule rather than a guess.

All of them on OpenReview.
